The risk premium, rather than deviations from purchasing power parity (PPP), explains most of the cross-country differences in real interest rates.

the main factor accounting for real interest rate differentiations across countries is the risk premium, while the deviations from the ex-ante purchasing power parity condition are marginal.
real interest rates are not equal across European countries because the risk premium is not equal across countries, but this does not imply that there is no convergence of real interest rates.
the real interest rate differential in Europe is not explained by the covered interest parity or purchasing power parity conditions but rather by risk premium factors.

the risk premium and deviations from covered interest parity are the main factors explaining the persistence of real interest differentials.
the risk premium plays a major role in explaining the differences in real interest rates across European countries, while the purchasing power parity plays only a marginal role.

real interest differentials are mainly driven by the risk premium.
real interest rates do not converge because of the risk premium.
